title: Grade 8 Science — Wed, Jun 18
description: Coal and Petroleum — Day 3 of 5: Formation of petroleum; refining; products
subject: science

questions.question: Petroleum is formed from:
options: Remains of tiny marine organisms (plankton, algae) buried under sea floors
questions.explanation: Petroleum (crude oil) formed from remains of tiny marine organisms (plankton, algae) buried under sea floors over millions of years under heat and pressure.

questions.question: What does 'petroleum' literally mean?
questions.explanation: Petroleum comes from Latin: petra (rock) + oleum (oil) = rock oil. It is called this because it is found in rock formations underground.

questions.question: The process used to separate different components of crude petroleum is called:
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation separates petroleum into fractions based on different boiling points — lighter fractions rise higher in the distillation column.

questions.question: In fractional distillation, which fraction has the LOWEST boiling point and rises to the TOP of the column?
questions.explanation: Petrol (gasoline) has the lowest boiling point of the major fractions and rises to the top of the fractional distillation column.

questions.question: Which petroleum product is used as fuel for cars (petrol engines)?
questions.explanation: Petrol (gasoline) is the primary fuel used in petrol/gasoline car engines.

questions.question: Which petroleum product is used as jet fuel?
questions.explanation: Kerosene (aviation turbine fuel/ATF) is used as jet fuel for aircraft engines. It is also used in kerosene lamps and stoves.

questions.question: LPG stands for:
questions.explanation: LPG = Liquefied Petroleum Gas. It is mainly propane and butane, liquefied under pressure, used in cooking cylinders.

questions.question: Which petroleum product is used for road surfacing (same as from coal tar)?
questions.explanation: Bitumen (asphalt) is the heaviest residue of petroleum refining. It is used for surfacing roads and waterproofing.

questions.question: Paraffin wax (from petroleum) is used to make:
questions.explanation: Paraffin wax is a solid fraction of petroleum used in making candles, wax coatings, cosmetics, and vaseline.

questions.question: Which of the following is the heaviest fraction from petroleum refining?
questions.explanation: Bitumen is the heaviest, highest-boiling fraction — it stays at the bottom of the distillation column and is a solid/semi-solid residue.

questions.question: Natural gas is mainly composed of:
questions.explanation: Natural gas consists mainly of methane (CH₄), with small amounts of ethane, propane, and butane.

questions.question: India's major petroleum-producing states include:
questions.explanation: Major petroleum-producing regions in India include Assam (oldest fields), Rajasthan (Barmer-Sanchor basin), and Mumbai High (offshore).

questions.question: Fractional distillation works because different petroleum components have different:
questions.explanation: Different petroleum fractions (petrol, kerosene, diesel, etc.) have different boiling points. Fractional distillation separates them by heating and collecting vapours at different heights.

questions.question: Which petroleum product is used to lubricate moving parts of machines?
questions.explanation: Lubricating oil (motor oil) is a petroleum fraction used to reduce friction in engines and moving machine parts.

questions.question: Petroleum is called 'liquid gold' because:
options: It is extremely valuable and fuels modern civilization
It is found alongside gold deposits
questions.explanation: Petroleum is called 'liquid gold' because of its enormous economic value and its role in powering transportation, industry, and modern civilization.
